previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and chronic heart failure was admitted for rapidly spreading painless blisters and erythema on the left foot, concerning for cellulitis. A CT scan ruled out abscess, necrotizing fasciitis, and osteomyelitis. He was started on IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, later transitioned to vancomycin and ampicillin-sulbactam. Podiatry performed lancing and drainage of the bullae. Wound culture showed mixed bacterial flora without anaerobes or resistant organisms. The patient was afebrile throughout and improved clinically. Due to concerns about antibiotic interaction, his warfarin was adjusted to 4 mg daily during antibiotic therapy. He was discharged home on oral Bactrim and Augmentin for seven days with detailed wound care instructions, despite declining home health support. Follow-up with podiatry was advised within two weeks.
